prompt:
The GAL-TAN framework identifies political orientation on a single axis. Individuals and texts are placed according to the degree to which their views align with either pole, as follows:

  - Individuals at the GAL (Green/Alternative/Libertarian) pole support expanded
    personal freedoms and social liberalisation, for example: access to abortion,
    same-sex marriage, environmental protection, and multiculturalism.

  - Individuals at the TAN (Traditional/Authoritarian/Nationalist) pole prioritise
    order, tradition, and stability, and believe that the state should treat the
    maintenance of national identity as a priority, for example: restrictive
    immigration policy, emphasis on law and order, defence of traditional social
    institutions, and national sovereignty over supranational authority.

A text occupies a position on this axis to the extent that it argues FROM these commitments, not to the extent that it mentions the associated topics:

  - Environmental or immigration policy discussed in administrative or fiscal
    terms does not by itself indicate a position.
  - Nuclear expansion argued for energy security is not GAL.
  - Faster asylum processing argued on humanitarian grounds is not TAN.

The profile below describes the positional priorities of the British electorate.

<profile>
  gal: 0.40
  tan: 0.60
</profile>

Below are two texts.

TEXT_D:
Reform UK’s 2024 “Contract with You” presents a rapid-change programme focused on cutting immigration, taxes and regulation; overhauling public services; expanding domestic energy; and constitutional shifts to assert UK sovereignty. The party frames the plan as an alternative to Conservatives and Labour, aiming to “take back control” of borders, money and laws.

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration and “stop the boats.”
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping care free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000 to “make work pay.”
- Scrap Net Zero policies and unlock UK oil and gas to cut bills.

Immigration
- Freeze non‑essential visas; create a Department of Immigration.
- Detain and deport illegal entrants; leave the ECHR if needed; process offshore; bar asylum from safe countries.
- Immediate deportation of foreign criminals; restrict student dependants; five‑year residency for benefits.
- Employer immigration tax (higher NI for foreign hires, with exemptions).

Government waste
- Stop Bank of England interest on QE reserves; 5% departmental efficiency drive; cut EU‑era rules; halve foreign aid; improve HMRC collection.

Economy (personal)
- Lift income tax start to £20k; higher rate from £70k.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p; scrap VAT on energy and green levies.
- Big stamp duty cuts; restore VAT‑free tourist shopping.
- IHT abolished below £2m; 20% rate above.

Economy (business)
- Raise corporation tax threshold to £100k; cut main rate to 20%, then 15%.
- Abolish IR35; lift VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs, offset with 4% online delivery tax.
- Looser employment rules; faster planning; major tax simplification.

NHS
- Zero basic‑rate income tax for NHS/care staff for 3 years; expand UK training and write off fees with service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if GP/consultant/operation waits exceed 3/3/9 weeks.
- Efficiency drives; pharmacy‑first approach; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms.

Net Zero/energy
- Scrap Net Zero and renewable subsidies; fast‑track North Sea and shale trials.
- Expand nuclear SMRs and other technologies.

Policing and justice
- 40,000 extra officers; zero‑tolerance approach; more stop and search; end DE&I roles.
- Increase justice budget; redefine hate crime; 10,000 new prison places; mandatory life for repeat violent offenders.

Education
- “Patriotic” curriculum; ban transgender ideology in schools; 20% tax relief on independent school fees.
- Scrap interest on student loans; tougher university standards; protect free speech; expand PRUs; offer 2‑year degrees.

Welfare
- Stronger work requirements (two‑strike rule); face‑to‑face assessments.

Brexit/sovereignty
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare TCA renegotiation; distance from EU defence ties.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay rises; new justice bill; veterans department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform.

Housing
- Fast‑track brownfield; prioritise locals in social housing; restore mortgage interest relief for landlords; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; protect leaseholders.

Families
- Transferable marriage allowance (aiming at 25%); front‑load child benefit for ages 1–4; single‑sex spaces; tackle social media harms.

Transport/utilities
- Scrap HS2; ban ULEZ/LTNs/most 20mph zones; invest in existing roads/rails.
- New ownership model: 50% public, 50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges.

Agriculture/fishing
- Boost farm budget; scrap climate‑linked subsidies; protect country sports; curb supermarket power; buy British.
- Restrict foreign access to UK waters; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers; rebuild processing and fleets.

Pensions/social care
- Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax avoidance in care; pension reforms; fix Mineworkers’ scheme.

Constitution/culture
- Leave ECHR; reform Lords and civil service; tighten postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Reject WHO treaty/WEF/CBDC; replace Equalities Act; free speech bill; scrap BBC licence fee; national holidays; anti‑corruption unit.

Funding (party estimates)
- Annual savings: ~£150bn plus £10bn from extra growth = £160bn.
- Annual costs: ~£141bn.

TEXT_G:
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2024 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core promise: A Fair Deal built on five themes — a stronger green economy, reliable public services, a cleaner environment, a fairer democracy, and a more outward-looking UK.

Economy and jobs
- Drive growth via a green industrial strategy, major investment in renewables, home insulation and skills.
- Fix EU relations, cut trade barriers, rejoin key programmes (Horizon, Erasmus) and aim long term to rejoin the Single Market.
- Support small business: abolish business rates and replace with a Commercial Landowner Levy; tackle late payments; expand British Business Bank; local banking.
- Fair taxes: reverse big bank tax cuts; proper windfall tax on oil/gas; raise Digital Services Tax to 6%; close CGT loopholes; 4% levy on FTSE-100 share buybacks.
- Workforce: replace apprenticeship levy with flexible skills levy; Lifelong Skills Grants (£5,000, aiming for £10,000); modernise gig-economy rights; fix sick pay; expand parental leave and pay.

Climate and energy
- Net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030.
- Ten-year emergency home upgrade: free insulation/heat pumps for low-income households; zero‑carbon standard for all new homes.
- Rooftop solar push; social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas; ban fracking and new coal; scale storage and interconnectors.
- Empower community energy; climate leadership abroad; end fossil fuel subsidies.

Health and care
- Legal right to see a GP within 7 days (24 hours urgent), recruit 8,000 more GPs; universal 24/7 booking; expand Pharmacy First.
- NHS dentistry: urgent and emergency access guaranteed; fix contracts; supervised toothbrushing; scrap VAT on kids’ toothpaste/brushes.
- Mental health: walk‑in hubs for young people; school mental health professionals; regular check‑ups; end out‑of‑area placements.
- Cancer: 100% treatment within 62 days; more radiotherapy machines; more cancer nurses; faster access to new treatments.
- Social care: free personal care; Carer’s Minimum Wage (+£2/hour); Royal College of Care Workers; paid carer’s leave and respite; cross‑party funding deal.

Education and families
- Per‑pupil funding to rise above inflation; fix crumbling buildings; Tutoring Guarantee for disadvantaged pupils.
- Early years: extra five free hours for disadvantaged 3–4s; triple Early Years Pupil Premium.
- Restore maintenance grants; Lifelong Skills Grants; teacher workforce plan; SEND funding reform; arts protected.
- Parental support: double statutory maternity/shared parental pay to £350/week; extra use‑it‑or‑lose‑it month for fathers at 90% pay; day‑one rights incl. self‑employed.
- Extend free school meals to all children in poverty.

Housing
- Build 380,000 homes a year, including 150,000 social; 10 new garden cities; use‑it‑or‑lose‑it permissions; Rent to Own model.
- Renters’ rights: ban no‑fault evictions; default three‑year tenancies; landlord register.
- Abolish leasehold; cap ground rents; remove dangerous cladding at no cost to leaseholders.
- End rough sleeping; scrap Vagrancy Act.

Nature and water
- End sewage scandal: transform water firms into public benefit companies; ban bonuses until discharges end; tougher regulator; Sewage Tax; real-time spill data.
- Double nature by 2050; 60m trees/year; Clean Air Act and new Air Quality Agency; stronger watchdogs (OEP, EA, Natural England).

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee police attendance and investigation of all burglaries.
- Cut court backlogs; Online Crime Agency; scrap Police and Crime Commissioners; end disproportionate Stop & Search; youth diversion nationwide.

Transport
- Accelerate EV switch: mass charging rollout, restore plug‑in grant, 2030 ZEV sales rule; cut VAT on public charging.
- Freeze rail fares; simplify ticketing; electrify rail; Northern Powerhouse Rail; empower councils to franchise buses; nationwide active travel plan; fix potholes.
- Reform aviation taxes; super-tax private jets; ban short flights where rail <2.5 hours (unless low/zero‑emission).

Immigration and asylum
- End Hostile Environment; scrap Illegal Migration Act and Rwanda plan; 3‑month target to process most asylum claims; allow work after 3 months; expand safe/legal routes.
- Merit‑based work visas; reverse family threshold hike; protect EU citizens; expand Youth Mobility.

Rights, democracy, defence, international
- Protect Human Rights Act; ban conversion therapy; scrap anti‑protest laws; flexible working right; right to work from home for disabled people.
- Proportional representation (STV) for MPs and English councils; votes at 16; cap donations; federal UK with written constitution.
- Defence: reverse Army cuts; target 2.5% of GDP; maintain nuclear deterrent; tighter arms export controls.
- Foreign policy: rebuild EU ties; support Ukraine (use seized Russian assets); restore aid to 0.7%; immediate ceasefire and two‑state solution, recognise Palestine; stand up to China/Russia; fund BBC World Service.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_G aligns more closely with this profile.

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",

  "winner": "TEXT_D" | "TEXT_G"
}
